[2026-01-13 01:55] lassoball : One way I think about it is for the first 5 or so seasons, HW is largely a recruiting game.  You’re slowly building a program of “your guys” while learning the game’s mechanics and what makes a good prospect.  When those first batches of recruits become upperclassmen and your starters, that’s really when the rubber meets the road.     I truly think D3 is one of the best times in HW.  You can’t demote, you’re learning, you’re probably taking chances on players that others have overlooked, which can be very fulfilling when they turn into productive players.

[2026-01-13 05:10] elvira883 : Another recruiting strategy is to 'sell out' for the future, especially relevant if the team you end up has 10/13 graduating or something. The consensus is to try to have like 3-4 roster spots open each season (not 1 and not 7 lol). And it doesnt mean you dont bring in 10 players. But that first season you redshirt the best few guys, plays the rest, and not worry if you end up 3-37 or something. An alternate strategy is do this for multiple seasons while trying to recruit the best HS FR and SO you reasonably can (3 star types) and then build normally behind them. The idea is build your team up for consistent success, rather than peak and get kicked back down immediately. And believe me, there are guys you can get for 1 contact that can make an impact in D3. Here were two of mine: https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/116216, https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/118259. Found them at practically the last minute in the 2022 recruiting cycle when I missed on everyone I was trying to land. If you have the only valid scholarship offer, or a recruit is more interested in your team than others on the day of their (usually hidden) commitment day, you get them even with just 1 contact. This is especially useful when the majority of the commitment cycle is over, for if their decision date has passed with no offers, you will get them next round. Note the 6'9. When in doubt, go tall

I suspect this doesn't update every training update.  So if you have an attribute that is displaying as 6 currently. But is actually a 5. [2026-02-01 15:15] naph7777 : "**__- Scouted Skill Values vs. Real Skill Values__**  **So are the skill values displayed for each player accurate?** Just as in real basketball, where there is some uncertainty about a player's talent level, in Hardwood there is also built-in uncertainty in displayed skill levels. The visible skill values for each player are an approximation of his current actual skill level and may deviate by up to 20% from it true value for some skills. Additionally, just like in real basketball, as a player plays more games, his displayed skill value will approach his true current skill level. Note, this may result in a player's displayed skill level actually dropping, even though he is receiving regular coaching and playing time. His skill value is not actually dropping, but because his actual skill level is better known now, a more accurate and lower value is now displayed."    https://onlinecollegebasketball.org/rules

[2026-02-24 01:48] eljefe7705 : I look at things on a positional basis. I rarely like my guards to be under 6'3" or below around 13/14 speed but I've had success with those that are a bit shorter like Braxton if they are elite elsewhere.  - PG, I prioritize passing, handling, spd, PD and shooting. I don't pay as much attention to IQ or DRV as some but like them to be solid on both. - SG has to be able to shoot and shoot deep, play PD, and be fast, with minimal exceptions.  - SF i usually like to be well-rounded so they can do a lot of different things so I look for more even distribution in skills. Usually like them to RBD too to give me a team advantage. Almost always want them 6'7" ish or above and not too heavy - PF doesn't need to be high in IS for me, have had plenty of really good PFs who can shoot. RBD and ID are musts with STR the other main priority along with decent spd. Like them to be at least 6'9" but preferably 6'10" 220+ lbs and wingspan over 7 feet - C is usually about ID, REB, STR, IS in that order but I've had shooters there too like Irish O'Connell. Like them to be at least 6'10" 230 lbs with a 7'2"+ wingspan

[2026-03-23 17:34] mdoman12 : Off the top of my head the important things to remember for actual evaluation of players is.   1. Expect a player to grow ~ 7 1/2” to 8 1/2” from his HS freshman starting height (so a guy who’s 6ft as a freshman should get to about 6’8.   2. Look at the overall dev in terms of SI to see how a player is actually developing as a player. My benchmark is you want to see them gain SI by their potential on average. So you’d like a 12 pot player to go +48 or better over his 4 seasons of hs.   3. Look at the dev graphs on a players page to see how their individual skills are progressing. This is helpful to see if he’s improving in the right skills. You’d want your PG prospect to see good growth in pass/BH where as for a big you might be looking for rebounding and interior defense.
[2026-03-23 17:36] mdoman12 : Those 3 steps should help you the most. After that it would be personal preferences and things that just are common sense like higher speed = good.
[2026-03-23 17:37] mdoman12 : I would also just read through the advice pins from Naph that show where you can expect ratings to be based on comments or SI caps

[2026-06-01 04:08] naph7777 : In general I try and have defenders at every position. Even though Balwin had the 6 ID he also had a 7' 7¼" wingspan and 34½" vert, so he wasn't a traffic cone or anything.
[2026-06-01 04:11] naph7777 : If you're playing teams that are guard-centric, particularly 3P-centric, and have low scoring bigs, then you can extend things out and not get punished as often. You also have to remember that fast break points are most often layups which impact your o2FG% disproportionately. So if your o2FG% sucks, but you're pressing or turning it over a bunch and giving up a bunch of layups, then maybe your halfcourt 2P-defense was fine, but the numbers are skewed by the FBP.
[2026-06-01 04:13] naph7777 : So generally with my settings I'm trying to work out what I want to try and take away/limit, and what I'm going to concede. Sometimes guys scorch you regardless of settings and you're better off limiting the supporting cast. Some guys are volume guys regardless of percentage and if you can make them have a tough shooting night you win. Some guys are capable of killing you with the pass if you try and take their shots away.
[2026-06-01 04:14] naph7777 : Every time I get tempted to say more than that.... I remember how many of my opponents will read this and kill me for it tactically 😛
[2026-06-01 04:16] naph7777 : But I do mix things up way more than I think most people do. I think SMC started the same extension only twice in a row in conference play last year. I lied, it was 3 times. And I'll have games with both teams where I'll swing from +3/4 to -3/4 in the same game for some matchups.
[2026-06-01 04:18] naph7777 : I'm sure that's part of why I get some horrific losses, but we also get some pretty amazing comebacks.... "tale of 2 halves" kind of games as well.
[2026-06-01 04:25] naph7777 : I think a default of negative extension makes the most sense for most teams in HW for a long time.  Most teams take significantly more 2's than 3's. They often also shoot the 2 more efficiently or close to the same efficiency as the 3 (especially true if you start factoring in FT's.... you get more FT's from shooting 2's than 3's). So it makes sense to make it hard inside, and just tip your hat if your opponent has a hot day from deep.
[2026-06-01 04:29] naph7777 : But once you start seeing teams with either dominant outside scorers, or a spread of guys who can all shoot 3's.... Particularly now that teams are capable of shooting 30 or 40 3's in a game. Those same teams might only be getting 20-25% of their FGA from their PF/C position combined. Is plan A against that team really going to be to crowd the paint and give their PF/C's a hard time? Half of their FGA are probably putbacks and you'll still be giving those up anyway. (Okay negative extension probably does help with both giving up less putbacks and defending them)
[2026-06-01 04:30] naph7777 : Anyway, that's enough monologuing/self-justification from me.
[2026-06-01 04:44] naph7777 : I'm sure part of it for me is just straight experimentation. If I'm going into a game thinking "Playing straight up I don't think I can win" or "I already have evidence I can't win that way", then I'd rather lose by a lot whilst trying something different, than just play the same way that I've lost before. I mean I'll still make plans to mitigate PD, because that can kill you too. But in conference games you might play a team 3 or even 4 times during the season. It worth having messed around a bit in conference so that when you're playing them in the CT or NT you have more idea of what works and doesn't work in that matchup.

[2026-07-22 03:16] naph7777 : I think everyone who has worked their way up to LL3 (at least without needing 5+ SR's in LL4) has a pretty good handle on  roster management and construction. What got you here may well not be enough to go higher. You need better builds, more star power or less flaws etc. That weaker part of your roster you didn't care about so much? Yeah, people keep poking you in that spot now. It hurts.  Remaining in LL2 I think you need a star most years. 5 really solid guys can work, but generally you end up with a down year and drop. Promoting from LL2 needs a critical mass of star players or a dream year with multiple guys overachieving.  Sticking in Legends requires another level of players and its pretty hard to maintain that level, especially if you strike out in recruiting at all. Most teams have a star player, if not 2. Someone probably has a roster that is a bad matchup for you. That said it does seem like there is usually a team or 3 that have gone all in to get to Legends and will drop back the next year. If you can get up without doing that, it might be enough to stick around for another year.

[2026-08-04 00:55] naph7777 : I think I'd rather spitball [this](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qaFKfbokWiBoxRPqo0otShXUK7Q1dWt5/view) in here before responding in the forums...  * Shot distribution - I assume there is a table something like this already in the game. I'm not 100% sold on the actual rates being published as I think this falls into the "good to have some mystery" part of the game. * Hard cap on 2 "I" guys I thought was to represent the fact that there are only 2 blocks to post up on. If you're the 3rd guy setting up at "I", then you're a 3-second violation waiting to happen. So if you set 3+ guys on "I", then at any given time you still only have 2 who are at "I" in effect and somebody gets pushed out to "i". * Driving effects on extended defense is interesting, in that I think it should make it harder to initiate a drive and get to the rim (so less frequency and higher TO%), but should also make it easier to finish when you do successfully drive (higher eFG%) * Bigger topic, but if you're going to have spacing like this you arguably need to introduce gravity as well. Setting  up a non-shooter (or worse non-scorer and non-passer) at "O" shouldn't provide as much spacing benefit as a flamethrower going for 20ppg on 40+% 3FG. Similarly the 2ppg 3topg C with hands of stone shouldn't suck the defense in much if at all. * I think the bigger issue will be that regardless of whatever we might come with as a community, Steve's going to have tinker with a game engine that is already in place. Depending on how it has been implemented not all ideas are going to be easy/feasible to integrate, and any large change like this would need a lot of testing before being rolled out.

[2026-08-10 19:51] eljefe7705 : Alright, so I did this (took way too long) across 12 categories. Figuring out the best way to paste it in but here are some interesting results for the 53 teams that have won Legends: - 9 have had the best eFG% and OeFG% - 8 had the best TO% and Opp TO% - Only 1 (2005 Vandy) had the best in all four - 4 had the fastest pace in the league, 3 had the slowest - The most 1st place ranks were eFG% (23) and Opp TO% (22)  - The least were blocks (3) and OR% (4) - 2010 Misericordia and 2020 Mississippi had the most #1 rankings with 7 - 2037 Temple was the only team not to finish 1st in one of the 12 categories - Winners only ranked last in a category 9 times with 2034 Alabama (TOV%, POSS) and 2048 Westfield (OeFG%, Opp TO%) doing it twice each. The other last place categories were blocks, OR%, and PITP - The best mean rankings were eFG% (3.04), Stl (3.25), Opp TOV% (3.26) - The lowest standard deviations were Stl (2.433), eFG% (2.682) and OeFG% (2.991) - The most volatile were Poss (4.565 std dev), OR% (4.063), Blk (4.008), FBP (3.945) - The 3 lowest average team ranks were 2005 Vandy (1.91), 2019 Mississippi (2.18), 2020 Mississippi (2.36).....and 3 lowest std dev's were 2005 Vandy (1.514), 2019 Mississippi (1.328) and 2037 Temple (1.809) - The 3 highest ranks were 2034 Bama (7.91), 2013 Tennessee (6.91), 2048 Westfield (6.55)....and 3 highest std devs were those same Westfield (5.956) and Bama (5.522) teams as well as 2040 Bama (5.045)

[2026-08-13 01:44] tcm12 : Something I found interesting that I would be interested to talk more about.  When using kenpom's formula for possessions per game (FGA - OR + TO + .475 x FTA), the top 7 teams in Legends all would lead NCAA DI in possessions per game.  In 2025-26, Cal Poly led the nation with an average of 78.3 possessions per game.  To use the highest number, Assumption averaged over 89, which is 10+ more than anyone in DI.  But if you look at DIII, Greenville, the NCAA PPG leader, averaged over 100 possessions per game.  I didn't realize there was such a difference in it between DI and DIII.  I initially thought that the game engine may have allowed for too up-tempo of offenses, but when you take into account that most people in this game run up-tempo, it may not be as crazy.  However, Youngstown State ran the entire season at 0 pace, but their possessions per game (73.6) would still be top 40 in all of NCAA DI.  But that may also be influenced by the fact that most people in the game play a faster offense.  I would be curious to hear people's thoughts on this, especially people who have done much more extensive research and analyzing in the game
